final_candidates.decision_summary: Mirrors the well-established natural OCT1 loss-of-function variant (R61C in canonical numbering), which strongly reduces metformin/TEA transport while protein remains expressed. Extracellular-loop arginine is not core to the fold, so viability risk is low.

stop_reason.detail: LLM-only iterative control with no external evidence; self-review indicates the Top-3 is stable and further rounds would not improve it.

history.rationale: Corresponds to the well-studied natural loss-of-function variant R61C in OCT1 numbering (this sequence lacks the initiator Met, shifting numbering by one; position 60 is indeed R here). This substitution strongly reduces metformin/MPP+ transport while the protein still traffics and is expressed at the membrane.

Corresponds to the well-known natural OCT1 loss-of-function variant R61C (1-position numbering offset), which strongly reduces metformin/TEA transport while the protein is still expressed at the plasma membrane. Arg60 in the large extracellular loop near TM1 disrupts substrate interaction without obviously destabilizing the fold.
Analogous to natural variant C88S, which reduces OCT1 transport activity while maintaining detectable protein. Ser preserves size/polarity, so folding risk is low.
